title: Choose the world for the CallGuard website
question: The roll dealt the Planisphere: the page is a star-finder wheel you turn through one night on a call. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Planisphere
options.lineage: printed star-finder wheels: a rotating sky disc under an oval horizon window, rimmed by hour and date scales
options.thesis: One night on a call, read off a star wheel. You turn the hour ring from 10 pm to 7 am, and each hour shows what CallGuard does at that moment of the night.
options.viewport: Full-width wheel cropped by the viewport. The oval window shows tonight's sky with CallGuard set large across it. The hour ring reads 10:00 PM at the pointer, and the Download for Mac button is set on the wheel's centre rivet plate, with View on GitHub beside it.
options.risk: Night-sky pages slide into 'near-black with glowing edges'. It must stay a printed instrument, with ink, tick marks and typeset numerals, and no neon.

raised.raise: One switch moves the whole sheet: flipping Mic Lock on the wheel turns every 'live' mark across the page to its locked state.
Every measured claim sits on the ring scales as an instrument reading in tabular figures (−64 dBFS leak at volume 0, 19 dB of ducking, 0.0% CPU idle).
One spot colour per hour of the night; everything else stays in the wheel's two inks.

options.label: On Air
options.lineage: late-night radio studios: the red ON AIR lamp, the backlit FM dial, the presenter's mic fader
options.thesis: Your mic is a broadcast. The ON AIR lamp is Mic Lock, and the glowing dial tunes the sound features.
options.viewport: A dark studio console across the viewport, a lit ON AIR lamp over the CallGuard name, the FM dial running underneath as the feature index, and the Download button as the console's big key.
options.risk: Familiar retro-radio territory, the direction most runs in this category land on, and it can read as nostalgia rather than a modern Mac app.

options.label: Glazier's Partition
options.thesis: Each feature is one pane in a black glazing grid; the pane you reach lights up in its own glass colour, echoing the app's Liquid Glass panel.
options.viewport: A glazing wall across the viewport, the CallGuard name in one big pane, Download in the lit cobalt pane.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: features map to panes and the active pane matches the app's glass. It wins on product clarity but loses on audience identification, because nothing in it says 'night on a call'.
options.risk: Can feel like architecture rather than a bedtime companion.

options.label: Miura-fold Sheet
options.case: Fuses poorly: neither the sleepy caller nor the feature list reads in a crease graph.
options.kept: One control propagates across the whole sheet.

options.label: Collider Event Display
options.case: Fuses poorly: lab spectacle, wrong audience; only the 8D orbit maps.
options.kept: Measurements as instrument readings in tabular digits.

options.label: Mid-century Magazine Program
options.case: Fuses poorly: an editorial program says nothing about calls or sleep.
options.kept: One spot colour per issue, with total discipline.

options.label: Calavera Broadside
options.case: Fuses poorly: skeletons and shouting type fight a calm bedtime app.
options.kept: The image band carries the section; the text is set hard beneath it.

options.label: Risograph System
options.case: Fuses poorly: a daylight zine on paper, the opposite of a night-time call.
options.kept: Two or three inks, total commitment.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished Mac app product page, executed impeccably: big headline, product screenshot, feature sections, download button.
canonCard.viewport: Centred headline and Download button over the real panel screenshot.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other Mac utility page; nothing says 'all-night call companion'.
